source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵי֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְיוֹסֵ֔ף הִנֵּ֥ה אָבִ֖יךָ חֹלֶ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־שְׁנֵ֤י בָנָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ אֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וְאֶת־אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after these things, and [someone] said to Joseph, look, your father [is] sick. And he took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.

en.L: And it happened after these things that [someone] said to Joseph, "Look, your father is sick." And he took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.
en.B: After these events, word came to Joseph that his father was sick, and he went, bringing his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
en.R: Some time after this, someone came to Joseph with news: "Your father is sick." So Joseph went to see him and took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, along.

decisions.choice: someone said: an unnamed messenger
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it means simply that word was brought to Joseph.

decisions.choice: Manasseh and Ephraim: Joseph's sons by his Egyptian wife
decisions.reason: They were born in Egypt before the famine (41:50-52). Manasseh, the older, is named first here, as birth order expects; the chapter will reverse that order.

decisions.choice: So Joseph went to see him
alternatives: he took his two sons with him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew implies the visit; Readable says it so the next verse follows.

source.text: וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה בִּנְךָ֥ יוֹסֵ֖ף בָּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יךָ וַיִּתְחַזֵּק֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב עַל־הַמִּטָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [someone] told Jacob and said, look, your son Joseph has come to you. And strengthened himself Israel and sat on the bed.

en.L: And [someone] told Jacob and said, "Look, your son Joseph has come to you." And Israel strengthened himself and sat up on the bed.
en.B: Jacob heard that his son Joseph had come to him, and Israel pulled himself together and sat up on his bed.
en.R: Someone told Jacob, "Your son Joseph is here to see you." So Jacob made himself strong enough to sit up in bed.

decisions.choice: Jacob ... Israel: two names for the same man
decisions.reason: The narrative moves between his birth name and the name God gave him (32:28; 35:10). Here "Israel" rises to act as head of the family before he gives the blessing.

decisions.choice: strengthened himself: summoned his strength
decisions.reason: The verb pictures an old, weak man making an effort, as the blessing he is about to give matters to him.

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Readable keeps one name in a single verse so young readers do not think two people are meant.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֵ֥ל שַׁדַּ֛י נִרְאָֽה־אֵלַ֥י בְּל֖וּז בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וַיְבָ֖רֶךְ אֹתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jacob to Joseph, God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in [the] land of Canaan and blessed me,

en.L: And Jacob said to Joseph, "God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
en.B: Jacob said to Joseph, "At Luz, in the land of Canaan, God Almighty appeared to me and blessed me.
en.R: Jacob said to Joseph, "God Almighty showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to me at Luz in the land of Canaan. He blessed me there.

decisions.choice: God Almighty: El Shaddai
decisions.reason: The title by which God made his promises to Abraham (17:1) and to Jacob (35:11). Jacob blessed Joseph's brothers with it before they went down to Egypt (43:14).

decisions.choice: Luz: the old name of Bethel
decisions.reason: God appeared to Jacob there twice, as he fled from Esau (28:10-19) and on his return (35:6-15). The words that follow repeat the second appearance (35:11-12).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י הִנְנִ֤י מַפְרְךָ֙ וְהִרְבִּיתִ֔ךָ וּנְתַתִּ֖יךָ לִקְהַ֣ל עַמִּ֑ים וְנָ֨תַתִּ֜י אֶת־הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את לְזַרְעֲךָ֥ אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ אֲחֻזַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and he said to me, look, I [am] making you fruitful and will multiply you, and I will make you into a company of peoples, and I will give this land to your offspring after you [as] a possession forever.

en.L: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, 'Look, I am making you fruitful, and I will multiply you, and I will make you into an assembly of peoples, and I will give this land to your offspring after you [as] a possession forever.'
en.B: He said to me, 'I am about to make you bear fruit and grow many; I will form an assembly of peoples from you, and I will give this land to your descendants after you, to hold as their own for all time.'
en.R: He told me, 'I will give you many children and make your family very large. Many peoples will come from you. I will give this land to your descendants after you. It will belong to them forever.'

decisions.choice: a company of peoples: an assembly made of many groups
decisions.reason: Qahal is a gathered assembly. The same phrase was in Isaac's blessing (28:3) and in God's words at Bethel (35:11). Jacob is about to make two tribes out of Joseph's sons, part of this promise coming true.

decisions.choice: a possession forever: land held for good
decisions.reason: The words of God's promise to Abraham (17:8). Jacob is dying in Egypt, but holds to the promise of Canaan.

decisions.choice: offspring
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "offspring" for zera, as in chapters 1-18; Balanced and Readable say "descendants".

source.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה שְׁנֵֽי־בָנֶיךָ֩ הַנּוֹלָדִ֨ים לְךָ֜ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם עַד־בֹּאִ֥י אֵלֶ֛יךָ מִצְרַ֖יְמָה לִי־הֵ֑ם אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ וּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כִּרְאוּבֵ֥ן וְשִׁמְע֖וֹן יִֽהְיוּ־לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And now your two sons, those born to you in [the] land of Egypt before my coming to you to Egypt, [are] mine; Ephraim and Manasseh, like Reuben and Simeon, they will be mine.

en.L: And now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh will be mine, as Reuben and Simeon are.
en.B: So your two sons, who were born to you in Egypt before I came to join you, are now mine. Ephraim and Manasseh will count as my sons, no less than Reuben and Simeon.
en.R: Your two sons were born here in Egypt before I came. Now I am making them my own sons. Ephraim and Manasseh will be counted as mine, just like Reuben and Simeon.

decisions.choice: they will be mine: Jacob adopts his grandsons
decisions.reason: Jacob takes Ephraim and Manasseh as his own sons, equal to his two oldest, Reuben and Simeon. Each will father a full tribe, so Joseph receives a double share, the portion of a firstborn (1 Chronicles 5:1-2).

decisions.choice: Ephraim and Manasseh: the younger named first
decisions.reason: In verse 1 the narrator named Manasseh first, by birth order; Jacob names Ephraim first, before the blessing puts him ahead (verse 20).

decisions.choice: Now I am making them my own sons
decisions.reason: Readable states plainly that this is an adoption.

source.text: וּמוֹלַדְתְּךָ֛ אֲשֶׁר־הוֹלַ֥דְתָּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם לְךָ֣ יִהְי֑וּ עַ֣ל שֵׁ֧ם אֲחֵיהֶ֛ם יִקָּרְא֖וּ בְּנַחֲלָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And your offspring whom you have fathered after them will be yours; by [the] name of their brothers they will be called in their inheritance.

en.L: But the children you have fathered after them will be yours; they will be called by the name of their brothers in their inheritance.
en.B: The children you have after them will belong to you; when the inheritance is shared out, they will be counted under their brothers' names.
en.R: If you have more children after these two, they will belong to you. They will receive their land as part of the share of Ephraim and Manasseh.

decisions.choice: called by the name of their brothers: counted under Ephraim and Manasseh
decisions.reason: Later sons of Joseph would not form tribes of their own; their land would come through the tribes of their older brothers.

decisions.choice: offspring: children
decisions.reason: The word here is moledet, those born to someone, not the word zera used in verse 4.

decisions.choice: as part of the share of Ephraim and Manasseh
alternatives: called by the name of their brothers
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom and names the brothers.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֣י׀בְּבֹאִ֣י מִפַּדָּ֗ן מֵ֩תָה֩ עָלַ֨י רָחֵ֜ל בְּאֶ֤רֶץ כְּנַ֨עַן֙ בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ בְּע֥וֹד כִּבְרַת־אֶ֖רֶץ לָבֹ֣א אֶפְרָ֑תָה וָאֶקְבְּרֶ֤הָ שָּׁם֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אֶפְרָ֔ת הִ֖וא בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, when I came from Paddan, died on me Rachel in [the] land of Canaan on the journey, while still a stretch of land to go to Ephrath; and I buried her there on [the] way to Ephrath, that [is] Bethlehem.

en.L: And as for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died, to my sorrow, in the land of Canaan on the journey, when [there was] still some distance to go to Ephrath, and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath" (that is, Bethlehem).
en.B: As for me, when I was coming back from Paddan, Rachel died on me in the land of Canaan, on the road, while we were still some way from Ephrath, and I buried her there by the road that leads to Ephrath" (that is, Bethlehem).
en.R: On my way back from Paddan, I lost Rachel. She died in the land of Canaan while we were still traveling, some way before Ephrath. That was a deep grief to me. I buried her there, near the road to Ephrath" (that is, Bethlehem).

decisions.choice: Rachel died: Joseph's mother
decisions.reason: Rachel died giving birth to Benjamin near Ephrath (35:16-20). Jacob remembers her as he adopts her grandsons; through them she gains two more tribes.

decisions.choice: died on me: a loss Jacob felt as his own
decisions.reason: The phrase "on me" can mean "to my grief" or simply "while I was with her". Either way it shows how the loss stayed with him.

decisions.choice: a stretch of land: some distance
decisions.reason: Kivrah is a measure of distance whose exact length is unknown; the same phrase is used of Rachel's death in 35:16.

decisions.choice: that is, Bethlehem: the narrator's note
decisions.reason: As in 35:19, the town is explained by its later, better-known name; the words are the narrator's, not Jacob's.

source.text: וַיַּ֥רְא יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִי־אֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Israel the sons of Joseph and said, who [are] these?

en.L: And Israel saw the sons of Joseph and said, "Who are these?"
en.B: Israel caught sight of Joseph's sons and said, "Who are these?"
en.R: Israel looked at Joseph's sons. "Who are these boys?" he asked.

decisions.choice: who are these?: a formal question
decisions.reason: Jacob could hardly see (verse 10). The question may also be part of the adoption: the father asks, and Joseph names them before witnesses.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־אָבִ֔יו בָּנַ֣י הֵ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־נָֽתַן־לִ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים בָּזֶ֑ה וַיֹּאמַ֕ר קָֽחֶם־נָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וַאֲבָרֲכֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joseph to his father, my sons [are] they, whom gave to me God in this [place]. And he said, bring them, please, to me, that I may bless them.

en.L: And Joseph said to his father, "They are my sons, whom God has given me here." And he said, "Bring them to me, please, so that I may bless them."
en.B: "These are my sons," Joseph told his father, "the ones God has given me in this place." Jacob said, "Bring them here to me, please, and I will bless them."
en.R: Joseph answered, "They are my sons. God gave them to me here in Egypt." His father said, "Please bring them to me. I want to bless them."

decisions.choice: whom God has given me: children as God's gift
decisions.reason: Joseph speaks of his sons as Jacob spoke of his own (33:5). He named them for what God had done for him in Egypt (41:51-52).

decisions.choice: here in Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable names the place.

source.text: וְעֵינֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כָּבְד֣וּ מִזֹּ֔קֶן לֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִרְא֑וֹת וַיַּגֵּ֤שׁ אֹתָם֙ אֵלָ֔יו וַיִּשַּׁ֥ק לָהֶ֖ם וַיְחַבֵּ֥ק לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] eyes of Israel were heavy from old age; not was he able to see. And he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.

en.L: Now the eyes of Israel were heavy with age; he could not see. And he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
en.B: Age had dimmed Israel's eyes, and he could not see. Joseph led the boys up to him, and he kissed them and held them in his arms.
en.R: Israel was very old, and his eyes were too weak to see. Joseph took the boys up to him, and Israel kissed them and put his arms around them.

decisions.choice: eyes heavy: failing sight
decisions.reason: Heavy eyes are dim eyes. Like his father Isaac, who could not see when he blessed Jacob (27:1), Jacob gives his blessing almost blind; but this time the old man knows exactly what he is doing (verse 19).

decisions.choice: he brought them near: Joseph
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he". Joseph is the one who brings the boys to his father, as verse 13 repeats.

decisions.choice: Joseph led the boys / Joseph took the boys
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who does what, since "he" could refer to either man.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף רְאֹ֥ה פָנֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א פִלָּ֑לְתִּי וְהִנֵּ֨ה הֶרְאָ֥ה אֹתִ֛י אֱלֹהִ֖ים גַּ֥ם אֶת־זַרְעֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Israel to Joseph, to see your face not I expected, and look, has let me see God also your offspring.

en.L: And Israel said to Joseph, "I did not expect to see your face, and look, God has let me see your offspring as well."
en.B: Israel said to Joseph, "I had given up hope of ever seeing your face, and look, God has shown me your children as well."
en.R: Israel said to Joseph, "I thought I would never see you again. Yet God has done even more: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has let me see your children as well!"

decisions.choice: I did not expect: I had given up hope
decisions.reason: Pillel here means to judge or reckon. Jacob had believed Joseph was dead (37:33-35).

decisions.choice: offspring
decisions.reason: Zera keeps "offspring" at Literal; the sense here is Joseph's children.

source.text: וַיּוֹצֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֹתָ֖ם מֵעִ֣ם בִּרְכָּ֑יו וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ לְאַפָּ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And brought out Joseph them from with his knees, and he bowed down [with] his face to the ground.

en.L: Then Joseph took them from his knees, and he bowed down with his face to the ground.
en.B: Joseph then moved the boys from beside his father's knees, and he bowed low with his face to the ground.
en.R: Then Joseph took the boys from his father's lap. He bowed down low with his face to the ground.

decisions.choice: from his knees: the sign of adoption
decisions.reason: To set a child on one's knees was a way of taking the child as one's own (30:3; 50:23). The boys had been on Jacob's knees; Joseph now takes them back to present them for the blessing.

decisions.choice: his knees: Jacob's
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "his knees"; it means the knees of Jacob, who had just embraced the boys.

decisions.choice: his father's
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whose knees, since the Hebrew pronoun could be misread as Joseph's.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח יוֹסֵף֮ אֶת־שְׁנֵיהֶם֒ אֶת־אֶפְרַ֤יִם בִּֽימִינוֹ֙ מִשְּׂמֹ֣אל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בִשְׂמֹאל֖וֹ מִימִ֣ין יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּגֵּ֖שׁ אֵלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Joseph the two of them, Ephraim in his right hand to the left of Israel, and Manasseh in his left hand to the right of Israel, and he brought [them] near to him.

en.L: And Joseph took the two of them, Ephraim with his right hand toward Israel's left, and Manasseh with his left hand toward Israel's right, and he brought [them] near to him.
en.B: Joseph set the two of them before his father: Ephraim, held in his right hand, at Israel's left, and Manasseh, held in his left hand, at Israel's right. Then he brought them up close to him.
en.R: Joseph led the two boys to his father. He held Ephraim with his right hand, so that Ephraim stood at Israel's left. He held Manasseh with his left hand, so that Manasseh stood at Israel's right.

decisions.choice: right hand: the place of the firstborn
decisions.reason: The right hand stood for strength and the greater honor. Joseph arranges the boys so that his father's right hand will fall on Manasseh, the firstborn.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל אֶת־יְמִינ֜וֹ וַיָּ֨שֶׁת עַל־רֹ֤אשׁ אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ וְה֣וּא הַצָּעִ֔יר וְאֶת־שְׂמֹאל֖וֹ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה שִׂכֵּל֙ אֶת־יָדָ֔יו כִּ֥י מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה הַבְּכֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And stretched out Israel his right hand and put [it] on [the] head of Ephraim, and he [was] the younger, and his left hand on [the] head of Manasseh; he crossed his hands, for Manasseh [was] the firstborn.

en.L: But Israel stretched out his right hand and put [it] on the head of Ephraim, though he was the younger, and his left hand on the head of Manasseh; he crossed his hands, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
en.B: Israel, though, stretched out his right hand and set it on the head of Ephraim, the younger boy, and his left hand on Manasseh's head. He crossed his hands knowingly, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
en.R: Israel stretched out his right hand and set it on the younger boy, Ephraim. He put his left hand on Manasseh's head. He had to cross his arms to do it, because Manasseh, the older son, stood on his right.

decisions.choice: crossed his hands: deliberately
decisions.reason: Sikkel is found only here. It is usually taken as "cross", but a word with the same letters means "act wisely", and both fit: Jacob crosses his hands knowingly (verse 19).

decisions.choice: for Manasseh was the firstborn: the reason the crossing was needed
decisions.reason: Because Manasseh stood on his right, Jacob had to cross his arms to reach Ephraim. The clause can also be read as "although".

decisions.choice: the younger before the older
decisions.reason: Again and again in Genesis the younger son is preferred: Abel, Isaac, Jacob, Perez (38:29), and now Ephraim. Blessing follows God's choice, not birth order.

decisions.choice: knowingly
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "knowingly" to carry the second sense of the verb (meaning decision m1).

source.text: וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֖ף וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ הִתְהַלְּכ֨וּ אֲבֹתַ֤י לְפָנָיו֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם וְיִצְחָ֔ק הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ הָרֹעֶ֣ה אֹתִ֔י מֵעוֹדִ֖י עַד־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he blessed Joseph and said, the God before whom walked my fathers Abraham and Isaac, the God who shepherded me from my [being] until this day,

en.L: And he blessed Joseph and said, "The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has shepherded me all my life to this day,
en.B: Then he blessed Joseph: "May the God in whose presence my fathers Abraham and Isaac lived, the God who has tended me like a shepherd from my birth until today,
en.R: Then he blessed Joseph with these words: "Abraham, my grandfather, and Isaac, my father, lived their lives serving God. And God has cared for me like a shepherd from the day I was born until now.

decisions.choice: he blessed Joseph: by blessing his sons
decisions.reason: The words that follow are spoken over the boys, yet the text says Jacob blessed Joseph: blessing Joseph's sons is blessing Joseph.

decisions.choice: walked before him: lived in his presence and service
decisions.reason: God had told Abraham, "Walk before me and be blameless" (17:1; see 24:40).

decisions.choice: who shepherded me: God as shepherd
decisions.reason: Jacob had been a shepherd all his life (30:31; 31:38-40). This is the first time in Scripture God is called the shepherd of a person; compare 49:24 and Psalm 23:1.

decisions.choice: Abraham, my grandfather, and Isaac, my father
decisions.reason: Readable says how each was related to Jacob, and breaks the long blessing into short sentences.

source.text: הַמַּלְאָךְ֩ הַגֹּאֵ֨ל אֹתִ֜י מִכָּל־רָ֗ע יְבָרֵךְ֮ אֶת־הַנְּעָרִים֒ וְיִקָּרֵ֤א בָהֶם֙ שְׁמִ֔י וְשֵׁ֥ם אֲבֹתַ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם וְיִצְחָ֑ק וְיִדְגּ֥וּ לָרֹ֖ב בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: the angel who redeemed me from all harm, may he bless the boys; and may be called in them my name and [the] name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they teem into a multitude in [the] midst of the earth.

en.L: the angel who has redeemed me from all harm, may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bless the boys; and in them may my name be called, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth."
en.B: the angel who has rescued me from every harm, bless these boys. Through them may my name be remembered, and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and may they teem and grow many on the earth."
en.R: He is the angel who has kept me safe from every harm. I pray that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bless these boys. Through them may my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac go on. May their families grow huge in number across the earth."

decisions.choice: the angel: God himself, as he met Jacob
decisions.reason: The angel stands in the same line as "the God" of verse 15, and the verb "may he bless" is singular: one being is meant. Jacob had met God through his angel at Bethel (31:11-13) and wrestled with him at Peniel (32:24-30; Hosea 12:3-4).

decisions.choice: redeemed: rescued as a kinsman would
decisions.reason: Go'el is the family member who buys back or rescues a relative (Leviticus 25:25; Ruth 4:4-6). Its first use in the Bible is here, of God.

decisions.choice: may my name be called in them: may they carry on the family line
decisions.reason: Through the two boys, now counted as Jacob's own sons, the family of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob continues.

decisions.choice: teem: multiply like fish
decisions.reason: The verb dagah is related to dag, "fish": may they become as many as fish in the sea.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: The angel is God (meaning decision m1), so the pronoun for him takes the deity pronoun setting. Balanced has no pronoun here.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא יוֹסֵ֗ף כִּי־יָשִׁ֨ית אָבִ֧יו יַד־יְמִינ֛וֹ עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וַיֵּ֣רַע בְּעֵינָ֑יו וַיִּתְמֹ֣ךְ יַד־אָבִ֗יו לְהָסִ֥יר אֹתָ֛הּ מֵעַ֥ל רֹאשׁ־אֶפְרַ֖יִם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Joseph that put his father his right hand on [the] head of Ephraim, and it was bad in his eyes; and he took hold of his father's hand to remove it from on [the] head of Ephraim to [the] head of Manasseh.

en.L: And when Joseph saw that his father had put his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it was displeasing in his eyes, and he took hold of his father's hand to move it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.
en.B: Joseph saw that his father had laid his right hand on Ephraim's head, and he did not like it. He took his father's hand, meaning to shift it off Ephraim's head and onto Manasseh's.
en.R: Joseph did not like seeing his father's right hand on Ephraim's head. So he reached for his father's hand to put it on Manasseh's head instead.

decisions.choice: it was bad in his eyes: he was displeased
decisions.reason: The idiom "in his eyes" means in his view. Joseph thinks his father has made a mistake because he cannot see.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶל־אָבִ֖יו לֹא־כֵ֣ן אָבִ֑י כִּי־זֶ֣ה הַבְּכֹ֔ר שִׂ֥ים יְמִינְךָ֖ עַל־רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joseph to his father, not so, my father, for this [one is] the firstborn; put your right hand on his head.

en.L: And Joseph said to his father, "Not so, my father, for this one is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head."
en.B: Joseph said to his father, "Not like that, my father! The firstborn is this one. Your right hand belongs on his head."
en.R: "Father, that is the wrong way!" Joseph said. "This boy is the older one. Your right hand should go on his head."

source.text: וַיְמָאֵ֣ן אָבִ֗יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יָדַ֤עְתִּֽי בְנִי֙ יָדַ֔עְתִּי גַּם־ה֥וּא יִֽהְיֶה־לְּעָ֖ם וְגַם־ה֣וּא יִגְדָּ֑ל וְאוּלָ֗ם אָחִ֤יו הַקָּטֹן֙ יִגְדַּ֣ל מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְזַרְע֖וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה מְלֹֽא־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And refused his father and said, I know, my son, I know; he also will become a people, and he also will be great; but his younger brother will be greater than he, and his offspring will become [the] fullness of the nations.

en.L: But his father refused and said, "I know, my son, I know. He too will become a people, and he too will be great. But his younger brother will be greater than he, and his offspring will become a multitude of nations."
en.B: But his father would not do it. "I know, my son, I know," he said. "Manasseh's line will also become a people, and it will be great as well. But his younger brother will rise higher still, and his descendants will fill whole nations."
en.R: But his father would not change his hands. "I know, my son, I know," he said. "Manasseh's family will also become a nation, and it will be great too. Even so, the younger brother will be the greater one. His descendants will fill many nations."

decisions.choice: I know, I know: Jacob is not mistaken
decisions.reason: The repeated word tells Joseph that the blind old man has crossed his hands on purpose. Long before, Jacob had deceived his own blind father to win the blessing of the firstborn (27:18-29); now he gives it to the younger son openly.

decisions.choice: the fullness of the nations: a great number of peoples
decisions.reason: The phrase means a mass of peoples. Ephraim became the largest tribe of the north, and later the northern kingdom itself was often called Ephraim (Isaiah 7:2; Hosea 11:8).

decisions.choice: Manasseh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Manasseh, since "he" alone could be unclear here.

source.text: וַיְבָ֨רֲכֵ֜ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֮ לֵאמוֹר֒ בְּךָ֗ יְבָרֵ֤ךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְשִֽׂמְךָ֣ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כְּאֶפְרַ֖יִם וְכִמְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־אֶפְרַ֖יִם לִפְנֵ֥י מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he blessed them on that day, saying, by you will bless Israel, saying, may make you God like Ephraim and like Manasseh. And he put Ephraim before Manasseh.

en.L: And he blessed them on that day, saying, "By you Israel will bless, saying, 'May God make you like Ephraim and like Manasseh.'" And he put Ephraim before Manasseh.
en.B: On that day he blessed them, saying, "Israel will use your name when they bless, saying, 'May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.'" In this way he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
en.R: So on that day Jacob blessed the boys. He said, "When the Israelites bless someone, they will speak your names. They will say, 'May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.'" So Jacob gave Ephraim first place, ahead of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: by you Israel will bless: your names will be used in blessings
decisions.reason: The "you" is singular, addressing each boy or the pair as one. Israel here is the people, who will bless their children by naming these two. Jewish fathers still bless their sons with these words.

decisions.choice: Israel: the nation to come
decisions.reason: The father named Israel speaks of the people who will bear his name.

decisions.choice: Ephraim before Manasseh
decisions.reason: The order of the names in the blessing settles the order of honor, as the crossed hands showed.

decisions.choice: you / your
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" is singular here but stands for both boys; Readable says "your names" so it is clear both are meant.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף הִנֵּ֥ה אָנֹכִ֖י מֵ֑ת וְהָיָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם וְהֵשִׁ֣יב אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ אֲבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Israel to Joseph, look, I [am] about to die, and will be God with you, and he will bring you back to [the] land of your fathers.

en.L: And Israel said to Joseph, "Look, I am about to die, but God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers.
en.B: Israel went on, speaking to Joseph: "My death is near. But God will be with you all and will lead you back to your ancestors' land.
en.R: Israel also told Joseph, "I am going to die soon. But God will be with all of you. He will bring you back to the land where your ancestors lived.

decisions.choice: you (plural): the whole family
decisions.reason: The "you" switches to the plural: God will bring all Israel back to Canaan. Joseph will repeat this promise before he dies (50:24).

decisions.choice: you all / all of you
decisions.reason: English "you" does not show the plural; Balanced and Readable add "all".

source.text: וַאֲנִ֞י נָתַ֧תִּֽי לְךָ֛ שְׁכֶ֥ם אַחַ֖ד עַל־אַחֶ֑יךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר לָקַ֨חְתִּי֙ מִיַּ֣ד הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י בְּחַרְבִּ֖י וּבְקַשְׁתִּֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I give to you one shoulder above your brothers, which I took from [the] hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.

en.L: And I give to you one ridge more than your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorites with my sword and with my bow."
en.B: And to you, more than to your brothers, I give one mountain slope, Shechem, the one I took from the Amorites by my sword and my bow."
en.R: And I am giving you one more share of land than your brothers: the ridge at Shechem. I took it from the Amorites with my sword and my bow."

decisions.choice: one shoulder: a ridge, and a play on the name Shechem
alternatives: one portion more than your brothers
decisions.reason: Shekhem means "shoulder", and so a mountain slope; it is also the name of the town of Shechem, where Jacob had bought land (33:18-20) and where Joseph would be buried (Joshua 24:32; John 4:5). The word may mean simply an extra portion, but the place seems in view.

decisions.choice: which I took with my sword and bow
decisions.reason: Genesis tells of no battle by Jacob for Shechem. Jacob bought land there peacefully (33:19), and he condemned the massacre his sons carried out there (34:30; 49:5-7). The words may refer to an event not told, or speak of what Jacob's house won as his own.

decisions.choice: the Amorite: the peoples of Canaan
decisions.reason: "Amorite" is often a general name for the inhabitants of the land (15:16).

decisions.choice: Shechem
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the place the word plays on (meaning decision m1). This goes beyond the Hebrew, which has only the common noun; Balanced says "mountain slope" for the word itself.
